# dsh-usage-heatmap

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web UI plugin: one
left-sidebar entry that opens a full-panel **calendar he

atmap** of daily session
and message counts, computed from the session logs this machine already sto

p** of daily session
and message counts, computed from the session logs this machine already stores.
## Features

- **A calendar, not a blank card.** Every day in the range is a visible square;
a stretch with no us

age still reads as a heatmap. Ranges: last 30 / 90 / 365
days, laid out as Monday-to-Sunday week col

umns with month and weekday labels.
- **Grid first, data later.** The calendar is painted from local

dates
immediately (a skeleton of pale squares), and the counts only repaint the
cells when they arr

ive. A failed load keeps the grid and shows the error
inline with a retry button.
- **Each day opens

up.** Selecting a cell expands a detail card below the
calendar: the message split (user vs assista

nt), sessions (active vs newly
created), tool calls plus the busiest tools, token usage (output and

cache
reads), the hour-by-hour activity shape with its peak, first/last activity and
its span, the w

orkspaces worked in, and the busiest sessions with their
titles. The day's two headline numbers come

from the calendar itself, so they
paint instantly; the rest arrives from a dedicated per-day detail

route.
- **Fast reopen.** Per-session day counts are cached on disk, so opening the
panel only re-r

eads sessions whose log file changed — normally just the
conversation being written. A background wa

rm-up runs a few seconds after
startup.
- **Account-scoped cache.** One cache file per DSH account,

so usage never leaks
across accounts.
- **Read-only and local.** Nothing is uploaded and nothing is

written outside
the cache. Colors come from `--dsw-alias-*` theme tokens, so light and dark
themes b

utside
the cache. Colors come from `--dsw-alias-*` theme tokens, so light and dark
themes both work.
### What it counts
| Field | Meaning |

| `sessions` | logical sessions whose header `createdAt` falls on that day |
| `messages` | `user/me
ssage` + `assistant/message` events whose own `time` falls on that day, across every session on the

machine |
| `detail` | for one selected day: user/assistant messages, active vs newly created sessio
ns, tool calls, token usage, hourly activity, workspaces, busiest sessions |

Events before a forked/subagent session's `inheritedEventCount` are skipped, so
an inherited log pre
fix is not counted twice.
## Install

This package is a DSH **profile bundle** (`dsh.bundle.patch` + `dsh.client`).
From a local checkout:

1. Quit DSH.
2. In the profile's `package.json` (for example
`~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json`)

add the dependency and list the
bundle:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

A git checkout works the same way — point the dependency at the cloned
directory.
3. Start DSH. The left sidebar gets the **使用热力图 / Usage heatmap** entry.

The checked-in `client.js` is already built, so a fresh checkout needs no
package install and no bui

ld to run. Only plugin development needs `pnpm`
(see Development).

> If you previously installed an auto-generated local version of this plugin,
> disable or remove th
at entry first so the sidebar only shows one heatmap.
## Cache and the HTTP routes

The Host half reads sessions through `ctx.sessionQuery` and serves two JSON
routes:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Cache files live under `$DSH_HOME/dsh-usage-heatmap/`:

- `cache-<account>.json` stores, per session, its message counts by day plus the
log file identity (

`mtime:size`) they came from.
- A request re-reads a session only when that identity changed; unchan

ged
sessions are reused, a disappeared session drops out, and a failed re-read
keeps the last good c

ounts.
- Delete the cache files to force a full rebuild; `refresh=1` rebuilds once.
### Day detail route
Selecting a day asks the second route for that day's breakdown. It reuses the same rolling cache to

decide which sessions were
active on that date, so a click re-reads only those logs — normally a han

dful —
instead of replaying the whole corpus. One response is bounded to the 150 most
active session

s of the day, plus the top tools, workspaces, sessions and models.
Titles and workspaces come from t

he session log itself (the latest
`session/title` event and the header `cwd`), and the client rememb

ers each
day's answer for the rest of the page session. A day detail request after the
calendar has

loaded does not rebuild the whole cache: it uses the same fresh
dataset the calendar request just wr

ed does not rebuild the whole cache: it uses the same fresh
dataset the calendar request just wrote.
## Repository layout
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The DSH Web client loads one lazy-CJS bundle per package (the `./client`
export), so `src/client/` i

s bundled ahead of time into the committed
`client.js`. The bundle only registers a factory with
`wi

ndow.__ModuleLoader__`, exactly like a compiled DSH client plugin. The Host
half is plain Node ESM a
nd runs straight from `src/host/`.
## Development
Requirements: Node.js (20+) and pnpm.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- **Client half:** edit `src/client/**`, run `pnpm run build`, restart DSH.
`client.js` is generated

— never edit it by hand.
- **Host half:** edit `src/host/**` and restart DSH; no build involved.
-

`node scripts/build-client.mjs --sourcemap` keeps function names readable and
emits `client.js.map`
for debugging (not committed).

The Host half writes its cache on the first request, so the first open after a
cold cache rebuild ma
y take a few seconds; later opens are incremental.
